PullRequest.Title: build: collect npm timings for Windows CI installs
PullRequest.Body:
Collect native npm timings during cold dependency installs in the Windows Browser, Electron, and Remote CI jobs.

- Enable `npm_config_timing` only for CI jobs with a test-suite flag.
- Send root and nested npm timing/debug logs to the absolute `.build/logs/npm` directory, included in the existing CI logs artifact.
- Preserve cache-hit skipping, install commands, retries, job budgets, and npm log level. Product builds and non-test compile jobs are unchanged.

Diagnostics follow-up to microsoft/vscode-engineering#3845.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold node_modules-cache miss in Windows Electron, Browser, or Remote CI test jobs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each job must complete the root npm ci, whose postinstall performs nested npm installs, before compilation and tests can proceed. The new npm timing/debug-log writes occur inside those npm processes and are therefore on the install critical path; publishing the existing logs artifact occurs during job finalization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Root and nested npm ci commands fetch dependencies from the configured npm registry on cache misses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One root install plus installs for the directories in build/npm/dirs.ts: up to 59 npm invocations when optional distro directories exist, separately in each of the three Windows suite jobs; package fetches remain subject to npm's own cache/deduplication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same root and nested npm installs and registry requests ran before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dependency fetches block completion of npm ci and therefore compilation/tests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: npm writes successful-run timing/debug diagnostics into the absolute .build/logs/npm directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one npm diagnostic stream/file set per root or nested npm invocation, bounded by the fixed directory list (up to 59 invocations per cold job) and task retries (initial attempt plus at most 5 retries).
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Successful npm installs did not force timing/debug diagnostics into the artifact directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These writes occur during npm installs and add bounded local I/O to the install critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The existing pipeline-artifact output uploads .build/logs, now including npm timing/debug logs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing log artifact publication per Windows suite job; payload grows with the bounded number and size of npm diagnostic files generated on cold installs/retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same artifact publication occurred, but without npm timing/debug files in its payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Publication happens as a job output/finalization action rather than before tests, but can extend total job completion time.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The fixed build/npm/dirs.ts list contains 56 install roots and may add 3 distro roots; timing output scales with those npm invocations and their dependency graphs, across three independently provisioned suite jobs. Cache hits reduce effective cardinality to zero because the Install dependencies task is skipped.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The three suite jobs are separate jobs. Within each job, build and remote installs are serialized to avoid node-gyp conflicts, while the remaining nested installs use a shared worker pool capped at 8. The changed logging does not increase process concurrency, though up to 8 npm processes per job can write separate logs concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cache@2 uses the computed package-lock cache key. On a warm node_modules cache hit, extraction occurs and npm ci is skipped, so the new variables produce no diagnostic files. On a cold miss, each affected suite job runs the installs and generates diagnostics; retries can add more files, but retry count is capped at 5. No new application cache or negative-cache behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed environment variables are scoped directly onto the cold-cache npm ci task, are inherited by the nested installs, and the existing artifact publishes their destination. There is no evidence that they change install concurrency, dependency download cardinality, or cache-hit behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact npm log byte volume and wall-clock overhead are not measured in the repository, and may vary with npm internals and dependency timing detail. The invocation count and critical-path placement are established, but the added work is the explicit, bounded purpose of this diagnostics change.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The diff intentionally collects bounded native npm timing data only on cold CI test-suite installs; the added filesystem writes and artifact bytes are concrete but necessary for the requested diagnostics, while install commands, concurrency, cache skipping, retries, and product-build paths are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Warm node_modules-cache hit in Windows Electron, Browser, or Remote CI test jobs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The cache archive is restored and extracted; the Install dependencies task is skipped by its existing condition, so the new npm timing configuration is not exercised.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: build/azure-pipelines/win32/steps/product-build-win32-compile.yml:68-72 and 116, cache extraction and install condition
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The existing node_modules cache archive is extracted; npm ci is skipped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cache extraction per job and zero npm timing-log producers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical cache extraction and install skipping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Extraction remains on the critical path, but the diff adds no work to it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One artifact publication per job, with no npm timing files generated by this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Job finalization only; no changed payload from npm timing on a cache hit.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One cache lookup/extraction per suite job; effective npm-install and timing-log cardinality is zero.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No root or nested npm installs execute. Existing extraction behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A matching Cache@2 entry sets NODE_MODULES_RESTORED=true, which skips the only task carrying the new environment variables. There is no changed cold-to-warm transition or cache key.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High, based on the unchanged task condition guarding npm ci.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for the changed mechanism; it is not reached.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance change on the warm-cache path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Windows product builds, non-test compile jobs, and smoke-flaky shared builds
Scenarios.CriticalPath: These workflows may still run npm ci on a cache miss, but the compile-time YAML condition does not emit npm_config_timing or npm_config_logs_dir because VSCODE_CIBUILD is false, no suite flag is set, or both.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing npm dependency installation on cache misses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged root and nested install cardinality for each applicable job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical npm install behavior because the new conditional block is absent from these expanded jobs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing install work remains on the build critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing dependency graph and fixed nested-install directory list; the changed timing-log cardinality is zero.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing npm postinstall concurrency remains unchanged; no changed diagnostic producers execute.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing Cache@2 hit/miss behavior and install skipping are preserved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the template parameters and callers: production jobs use VSCODE_CIBUILD=false, while smoke-flaky does not set an Electron/Browser/Remote suite flag.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material because the conditional excludes these scenarios.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance change; the new diagnostics are excluded.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete one-file diff and traced all template callers, cache conditions, nested npm-install fan-out, concurrency, local log writes, registry access, and log-artifact publication. The change adds bounded, intentional diagnostic I/O only to cold Windows Electron/Browser/Remote CI installs. No high-confidence actionable performance bug was found.
